# Heatmap / matrix

Contents: [Use cases](#use-cases), [Chart IDs](#chart-ids), [Minimal spec](#minimal-spec), [Data](#data), [Options](#options), [Annotations](#annotations), [Sizing](#sizing), [Fixtures](#fixtures).

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-reference.mjs from the boardplot describe, list and fixtures payloads. -->

Row × column matrix — continuous or discrete color scale, in-cell values or Harvey balls. Type `heatmap`. Aliases: `matrix`.

## Use cases

- A value by row and column
- Harvey-ball scoring
- Sales by weekday and hour

## Chart IDs

- `heatmap.value`: fixture `regional-monthly-performance`
- `heatmap.harvey`: fixture `harvey-quarter-steps`
- `heatmap.bubble`: fixture `survey-journey-bubbles`

## Minimal spec

```json
{
  "type": "heatmap",
  "data": {
    "categories": [{ "id": "jan", "label": "Jan" }, { "id": "feb", "label": "Feb" }],
    "series": [
      { "id": "north", "label": "North", "values": [80, 95] },
      { "id": "south", "label": "South", "values": [65, 85] }
    ]
  },
  "options": {
    "unit": "orders",
    "title": "Orders rise in both regions in February",
    "source": "Illustrative data"
  }
}
```

## Data

A `cell` is a number, null or a value object; see [Value cell](options.md#value-cell).

| Path | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| valueKind | string |  | Default valueKind for all series. One of `'fraction'`. |
| categories | array | yes | Matrix columns in display order; each series supplies the values for one row. |
| categories[].id | string | yes | Category identity used to match keyed values and annotation anchors. |
| categories[].label | string |  | Displayed category name; defaults to the category id and supports line breaks. A date id or `date` without a label prints a short date such as '4 Sep'. |
| categories[].date | string |  | Accepted ISO 8601 date metadata; heatmap columns remain category bands. |
| categories[].footnote | integer |  | 1-based reference into options.footnotes. The number is drawn beside this category label as the reference mark, and the note it points at keeps that number; a reference to no note draws nothing and warns, and notes the engine derives print unnumbered. |
| series | array | yes | Matrix rows, each supplying one cell value per category. |
| series[].valueKind | string |  | Multiply numbers by 100 into pct cells; explicit pct cells stay in percent units. One of `'fraction'`. |
| series[].id | string | yes | Series identity used by keyed options, annotations and legend entries. |
| series[].label | string |  | Displayed series name; defaults to the series id. |
| series[].values | (cell \| { categoryId, value: cell })[] | yes | Values in category order, or keyed entries pairing a categoryId with its value. |
| series[].scenario | string |  | AC, PY, PL, FC (or ACT, BUD, FCST). Controls scenario labels and paint conventions. |
| series[].direction | string |  | Declares this row's judgment for the continuous scale and PINS the whole matrix on the good/bad valence ramp (like table heat's signed flag) — declaring 'higherIsBetter' is therefore not a paint no-op on an all-positive matrix. 'lowerIsBetter' inverts the row's poles. Breaks bins go bad to good; under a breaks key every row needs the same direction (else refused). Ignored by the plain discrete ladder and harvey glyphs (warned). One of `'higherIsBetter'`, `'lowerIsBetter'`. |
| series[].colorRole | string |  | Accepted series color role; heatmap colors are resolved by the matrix scale and cell fills. One of good, bad, warn, neutral, neutralLight, highlight, total, others; series-N for step N of the theme ramp, 1-based (series-2 is color.series[1]); or status-<key> for a theme status colour. A hex colour goes in fill. |
| series[].unit | string |  | Unit shown with this series values and used to check shared-scale compatibility. |
| series[].format | string |  | Format-by-example for this series values, for example 1,234 or 1.2%. |
| series[].sizes | array |  | Bubble sizes. One per category, in order: a level 1 to n with bubble.levels, else area ∝ size. |
| series[].bases | array |  | Cell bases (n). One per category, in order; below minBase draws hatched. |

## Options

| Path | Type | Values | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| scale | string | `'continuous'`, `'discrete'` | `'continuous'` | Continuous color interpolation by default, or a discrete color ladder. |
| variant | string | `'value'`, `'harvey'`, `'bubble'` | `'value'` | Value labels fit as a whole row; authored labels and valid pins retain precedence. Harvey glyphs suppress values and take ratings 0 to 4 only; any other value is refused. 'bubble': one circle per cell, colour = value, area = series sizes; values print where they fit. |
| cap | object |  |  | Where the continuous scale saturates, as table heat's cap: a value at or past it paints full strength, measured from zero. Without it the good/bad scale is symmetric, full at the largest \|value\|, and the magnitude ramp spans the data. The discrete ladder and harvey glyphs ignore it (cap-ignored). |
| cap.pct | number |  |  | Cap in points when every cell is a percent. Example: 20 saturates at ±20%. |
| cap.abs | number |  |  | Cap in source units for other values. |
| breaks | array |  |  | Bin edges. Ascending, for scale 'discrete', e.g. [0, 30, 50, 100]; an edge value takes the upper bin. A series direction paints bins bad to good. |
| bubble | object |  |  | Bubble glyph. Its keys stand above the matrix; legend 'none' drops them. |
| bubble.levels | array |  |  | Size levels. Names smallest first, e.g. ['Low', 'Medium', 'High']; sizes hold levels 1 to n. |
| bubble.sizeLabel | string |  |  | Size key title. |
| bubble.colorLabel | string |  |  | Colour key title. |
| bubble.track | boolean |  |  | Row track. A line with an arrow through each row; implies ordered columns. Default false. |
| minBase | number |  |  | Low-base threshold. Cells whose series bases entry is below it draw hatched, with a note. |
| missing | string | `'hatch'`, `'blank'` |  | How a cell with no value is drawn. 'hatch' (the default) stripes the cell and names it in the key. 'blank' draws no fill and no stripe; the same key entry or note still says that a blank cell is no data. A blank cell keeps its grid line and dash, so it does not read as the palest value. A low base (bases and minBase) stays hatched. |

Plus the [shared options](options.md). This type does not accept `categoryLabels`, `valueAxis`, `categoryAxis`, `secondaryAxis`, `rowLabels`, `topN`, `bandFraction`, `rounding`.

## Annotations

An annotation anchor is a category or item id string, or an object with categoryId plus optional seriesId, segmentId and edge (start, end, total); pointId addresses a scatter point. Category anchors, including from/to, take category ids, not category labels.

| Kind | Purpose | Required | Anchors | Optional fields | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| cagr | Draws a growth arrow between two anchored points and computes the compound annual growth rate from their values and ISO-date span. |  | from: AnchorRef (optional); to: AnchorRef (optional) | suffix: string, default 'p.a.'. Text after the rate. period: boolean. Print the period before the rate from the anchors' category labels, '2014–2019: +5.8% p.a.'. Default true when the chart carries two or more CAGRs, so nested brackets are told apart by their text, false otherwise. | Omitted endpoints span the first to the last category, or the first to the last total on a waterfall. Resolved endpoints need a positive date interval from ISO dates or year-bearing labels and a positive start value; an end of zero reads -100%, and a start at or below zero or a negative end omits the rate and warns cagr-undefined. On a continuous time axis the years are the exact span between the two readings. An anchor on one series of several (seriesId, or a line category, which reads the first drawn series) names that series in the label, "Product B +10.1% p.a.", and the arm runs from that series' segment or point. In text, ${value} prints the rate with its suffix, so "CAGR 2014–2019: ${value}" keeps the computed number. |
| diff | Draws a level-difference arrow between two anchors and computes either percent change or their signed value difference. | from, to | from: AnchorRef; to: AnchorRef | mode: relative \| absolute \| reversed, default relative. relative prints the percent change from 'from' to 'to', reversed the change from 'to' to 'from', absolute the value difference. | Mode defaults to relative. Relative and reversed changes need a nonzero base; negative bases use its absolute magnitude and emit a warning. Absolute mode reports the raw value difference. A hidden label removes its arm. |
| callout | Places authored free text at an anchored data element, routing a leader when displaced and honoring the preferred side. | at, text | at: AnchorRef | preferSide: left \| right \| above \| below. Side the solver tries first; the label keeps a leader when it moves. headline: string. A bold first line over the text, which then prints in plain type; ${value} in it prints the anchored value from the data. Example: "headline": "${value}", "text": "Peak in handheld-loom demand" prints 153 in bold over the words. arrow: boolean, default false. A thin arrow from the text to the anchored point; the first line sits level with the point, right or left of it, where there is room. Not with icon or status. Example: "arrow": true. |  |
| note | Places authored text at an anchored data element through collision avoidance, with an optional icon or status chip. | at, text | at: AnchorRef |  |  |
| delta | Computes the signed difference between an anchored value and another anchor or literal, then places a collision-managed label at the first anchor. | at, vs | at: AnchorRef; vs: AnchorRef \| number |  |  |
| abs | Reads the anchored data value and places its formatted absolute value in a collision-managed label. | at | at: AnchorRef |  |  |

## Sizing

Floor 280 × 28 px; fit `content`.

Below the floor a render is refused with `size-below-floor` and the pixels it needs. `measure` returns the natural and comfortable size for a given spec; see [Sizing in the manual](../manual.md#sizing).
